Paklibychme tobo neuczinili a nezdrzeli, a toho zbozie swrchupsaneho se wssim przislussenstwim, aneb kterebo kusu zwlasstie nezprawili, neoczistili a newyswobodili, aneb zpra- witi, oczistiti a wyswoboditi nehmoli, tehdy my zprawcze a rukoy- mie swrchupsanij mameaslibugem wierzitelom nassim swrchupsanym tak dobry puoziteczny dwuor popluznij wes y mlyn s platem, s gich przislussenstwim, s takuz dobru zwolij swobodnu, iakoz se swrchu. pisse hned na nassich kruntech diediczkych swobodnyeb a zbozij wlastnim dobrym platnym swobodnym a dobrze vsedlym, y trzefinu wysse k tomu przicziniecze bez odpornosti postupiti a to take Ygi- stiti, zprawiti, oczistiti a wyswoboditi a wedsky zemske wloziti, zapsati, a vtwrditi ku prawemu gich diedicztwij a plnemu panstwij a zprawcze hodne postawiti tak, iakoz se swrchupisse. Paklibychom tobo neuczinili aneb ktereho koliwiek kussu w tomto listu zapsaneho a polozeneho nenaplnili, tehdy my zprawcze a rnkoymie swrchup sanij mame, a slibugem beze wssie omluwy, kdyz a kterziz naipnv od wierziteluow nassich swrchupsanych na pomenuti budem listem poslem neb vstnie, lmed nazaitrzie wgeti a wlehnuti kazdy sam osebnie s gedniem pacholkem a se dwiema konioma, anebo miesto sebe kazdy z nas w to lezenie bude moczi poslati a wloziti panossi rzadu rytierzskeho tez s gedniem pacholkem a se dwiema ko nioma do miesta Krumiowa , anebo do gineho miesta, neb miesteczka w pieti neb w ssesti milech wzdali, nebo blize w zemi Czeske w duom cztneho hospod,arze, tu kdez nam od wierziteluow nassich swrchupsanych bude pokazanoaneb gmenowano. A tu prawe a obyczeyne lezeni plniti a westi mame, a slibugem podle rzadu a obyczege zemie Czeske, a odtud nikam na nizadne prawo newygezdieti aniwychoditi, ani kterym obyczegem toho lezenie pra- zdni byti ncmame tak dluho, dokudz bychom toho wsseho neuczi nili, czoz tento list swiedczij a wypisuge. A kdyzby minulo cztrnadczte dnij od napomenutie k tomu lezenie rownie porzad cztucze, lezme my nebo nelezme, a gestli ze bychom tobo wssebo neuczinili aneb ktereho kusu nenaplnili, czoz se pisse w tomto 357 listu, tehdy dawame tiemto listem plnu mocz y prawo w erzitelom nassim swrchnpsanym tiech ssest seth zlatych Vherskych dobrych, a trzetinu wysse k tomu przicziniecze wzieti a dobyti wKrzestianech nebo w Zidech na nassy wssech rukoymij sskodu spolecznij a neroz- dielnu.a kdez ge koliwiek optagi a wezmu w zemi Czeske, tu my ge mame a slibugem zastati peniezi swymi hotowymi, aneb nassimi zaklady aneb rukoymiemi hodnymi, tak aby wierzitele nassy w torn nizadne sskody nemieli. Pakliby wierziteie nassi czastopsanij skrze nasse neplnienie a nezdrzenie, ktere sskody wzali, kterezby prostymi slowy bez przisah a wierowanie pokazati mohli, takowe wsseczky sskody slibugem gim zaplatiti peniezi hotowymi, z toho lezenie newinikugicze do koneczneho wywazenie, zaplaczenie a dosti vczinienie. Vmrzelliby take kto z nas z prawczij a rukoymij swrchupsanych , neb gistecz w tom czasu, gehoz pane boze racz ostrzieczy, tehdy my ziwij zuostalij mame a slibugem w gednom miesieczy naiblizssiem porzad zbiehlem a po napomenutie miesto toho vmrleho gineho tak dobreho a mowiteho k sobie w tuz z prawu a rukogemstwie przistawiti, a list tento w taz slowa obnowiti, kolikratby toho potrzebie bylo, pod lezenim swrchupsanym. A ktozby tento list miel s nadepsanych wierzitelow nassich dobru wolij swo- bodnu, ten tez prawo y tuz mocz ma a mieti bude k tomu kewssemu, czoz swrchupsano gest, iakozto oui sami.Tomu wssemu na potwrzenie a lepsij gistotu y pewnost my wssiczkni gistecz y zprawcze a rukoy- mie swrchupsanij wlastnie nasse peczet s dobrym nassim wiedomim a plnym y czelym prziznanim dali sme a kazali prziwiesiti k tomuto listu dobrowolnie. Genz gest dan na Krumlowie leta od narozenie syna bozieho tisiczieho cztirzsteho osmdesateho sedmeho tu sobothu przed swatu Alzbiethu. entries.english:
I, Peter von Rosenberg, guardian of the orphans and children of the late Ondřej of Nemyšl, declare by this letter to all, publicly and before everyone who sees it or hears it read, that after careful deliberation and counsel I have sold and, by this instrument, do sell and convey in rightful inheritance and full possession the farm estate at Rowna, the village of Rowna, and the mill, with farmsteads, tenants’ holdings, rents, labor services, hens, fishponds, streams, cultivated and uncultivated lands, meadows, woods, scrubland, pastures, commons, and every appurtenance, however it may be named, just as I held and used it in the guardianship of those orphans and as its ancient boundaries have long established. I reserve no right or privilege in it for myself, the said orphans, or our heirs and successors. I convey it to the honorable Wenceslas, my chancellor, and his heirs for six hundred good Hungarian gold florins, of the proper weight and assay, which he has paid me in full. After being summoned, I shall on the first court day, or the second if necessary, and no later than the third, enter and record the farm, village, mill, and appurtenances in the land books, establish them securely in his rightful inheritance and full possession, and provide proper warranty according to the law of Bohemia, without dispute.

For greater security I have provided as guarantors and sureties the noblemen Cunrath of Petrowicz, Peter von Drbrohostie der Jüngere, Burggraf zu Krumau, Waclaw of Zhorze, and Gindrzich Sudek of Dluhe. We, the persons named as guarantors and sureties, jointly and severally pledge our good Christian faith that we shall warrant the farm, village, and mill to our creditor, clear and free from all claims, orphans’ rights, records, and encumbrances, whether Christian or Jewish, and from the claims of any person, ecclesiastical or secular, of whatever rank or estate. If we fail to do so, or cannot clear or free the whole property or any part of it, we shall convey to our creditor an equally good and profitable farm, village, and mill, with appurtenances and equally good freehold, from our hereditary estates and property, and add a third more, without objection; we shall also secure and record it in the land books for his rightful inheritance and full possession, and provide proper warranty as above.

If we fail to fulfill any part of this letter, then, without excuse, whenever our creditor summons us by letter or orally, each of us shall promptly go into customary confinement, personally with one servant and two horses, or send in his place a nobleman of knightly rank with one servant and two horses. We shall go to Krumau, or another town or small town within five or six miles, to the house of an honorable host designated by our creditor. We shall remain there in proper and customary confinement, under the law and custom of Bohemia, and shall neither depart nor evade confinement by any means until we have fulfilled everything witnessed and stated in this letter. If fourteen days have passed after the summons to confinement, counted consecutively, whether or not we have entered confinement, and we have not fulfilled all or any part of this letter, we hereby grant our creditor full power and right to recover the six hundred good Hungarian florins and an additional third from all of us as guarantors, jointly and severally, wherever he can find us in the Christian or Jewish communities of the kingdom of Bohemia. We shall reimburse him with ready money or suitable pledges and sureties so that he suffers no loss. We also promise to pay in cash every loss our failure has caused him, if he can show it in plain words, without oath or formal proof, until full settlement, payment, and satisfaction, without thereby releasing us from confinement.

Should any of the guarantors or sureties, or the principal debtor, die during this period—which God forbid—we survivors promise, within the next calendar month after notice, to provide in place of the deceased another person of equal standing and means as guarantor and surety under the same terms, and to renew this letter in the same wording as often as necessary, subject to the confinement obligation above. Whoever holds this letter with the free and willing consent of our said creditor shall also have the same right and authority to all the foregoing as the creditor himself. In confirmation and greater assurance, all we guarantors and sureties have voluntarily ordered our seals attached to this letter, with our knowledge and full consent. Given at Krumau on the Saturday before Saint Elizabeth’s Day in the year 1487.

Five small seals hang from parchment strips: one in red wax and the others in black. They bear the arms and names of Peter von Rosenberg, Kunrat of Petrowicz, Peter of Dobrohostie, Waclaw of Zhorze, and Gindrzich of Dluhe. The parchment strips are labeled with the sealers’ names.
